关键词: U.S. Treasury Secretary Jacob J. Lew
主要内容: On June 7, 2016, U.S. Treasury Secretary Jacob J. Lew and Chinese Vice Premier Wang Yang concluded the eighth U.S.-China Strategic and Economic Dialogue (S&ED). The S&ED, established in 2009, has served as a platform for the two sides to make progress on core issues in the economic relationship. The U.S. Administration secured actions from China that level the playing field for U.S. workers and firms, deepen cooperation on global challenges such as climate change, and promote critical market-oriented reforms in China. At this year’s S&ED, the Administration built on this foundation to secure new and strengthened commitments that will ensure China’s economic growth continues to deliver concrete benefits for the American people, including through furthering China’s exchange rate reforms, addressing excess industrial capacity, promoting non-discriminatory trade and investment measures, improving economic transparency, and advancing policies to shift China’s growth model to one driven by household consumption rather than investment and exports. The U.S.-China Strategic and Economic Dialogue, held on June 7, 2016, focused on economic cooperation and reforms. China committed to rebalancing its economy toward household consumption and services, while ensuring private sector-driven investment. Short-term measures included proactive fiscal policies to expand domestic demand. The social safety net was to be strengthened through improved local taxation, enhanced medical and pension benefits, and sustainable social security funds. Factor price liberalization was also a key area, with commitments to liberalize prices in sectors like electricity, petroleum, and transport. The U.S. obtained China's commitment to increase SOE dividend contributions and improve transparency. Addressing excess steel capacity was a priority, with China outlining structural reforms to reduce overcapacity and align fiscal incentives. The U.S. and China also agreed to improve the approval process for agricultural biotechnology products, aligning with previous agreements from the 2015 State Visit. The discussions focused on enhancing economic cooperation, with key areas including improving aviation system efficiency, increasing corporate information transparency, and promoting equal treatment of foreign and domestic enterprises in industrial policy. China committed to publishing draft plans for industrial development funds and ensuring market-based operations. The dialogue also addressed expanding RMB trading and clearing capacity in the U.S., with both nations agreeing on a policy framework to support this. Additionally, the U.S. and China reached agreements on strengthening regulatory cooperation and information-sharing to support global financial stability. China announced plans to issue licenses to U.S. banks for underwriting corporate bonds and serving as bond settlement agents, marking a significant opportunity for foreign investors. Key commitments included regulatory reforms in China to allow foreign futures exchanges to establish representative offices and simplify administrative procedures in its securities markets. China also committed to expanding access for foreign institutional investors, enhancing financial transparency, and strengthening corporate governance. Both nations agreed to cooperate on regulatory matters, including cross-border enforcement and information sharing. The U.S. and China reaffirmed their commitments to the Financial Stability Board’s total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) standard for global systemically important banks (G-SIBs). Additionally, they pledged to work together on global challenges such as export credit guidelines and low-carbon technologies.
